pages.text: In quantum field theory an $(thing)anomaly$() is a technical word: a symmetry that holds in the classical theory and fails in the quantum one. The chiral charge of massless fermions should be conserved; in parallel electric and magnetic fields it is created from the vacuum at the rate e²E·B/2π² per unit volume. This $(thing)anomaly$() is real - it makes the neutral pion decay into two photons, and it is measured in crystals today.

So normality can be broken locally, by exactly calculable amounts, without the rest of physics falling apart: the theory as a whole stays consistent because the anomalies of different particles cancel. Where a defect core touches ordinary space, such violations leak out.

In the $(item)Anomaly Containment Ward$(), a Topological Defect Core, specimens and a Law Crystal in primordial law leave $(item)Local Law Violations$(): small regions where a conservation law quietly fails.
